solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good looks of workman with quite a head

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand
'that's some car' means quite a car, so quite a gives some
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A labourer is admired for his good looks and his impressive head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite a head' reads as praise for the workman's skull; 'quite a' is the idiom 'that's some...', and a ness is a headland, as in Scottish place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Being handsome is having good looks, so the abstract noun for that quality fits.

clue.text: Throat intermittently before examination is most inflamed

indicators.note: intermittently means taking every other letter of throat

parts.note: a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A doctor's check shows which sore throat is the worst inflamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed tissue is red and hot, so the most inflamed is the hottest.

clue.text: Desperate man rises, hugging fine fantastic girl

indicators.note: hugging means the reversed name wraps round the next letters
rises means the name is read upward, which in a down entry is backwards

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy
AI, as in A1, means first-class or fine

explanation.surface: A frantic man stands and embraces a lovely, imaginary girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a cowpie-eating giant from the long-running British comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, a girl from fantasy.

clue.text: Return of Queen, portion's included for release

indicators.note: included means the reversed letters are placed within the portion word

parts.note: a section is a portion or part

indicators.note: Return of means the royal letters are reversed

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen comes back and a portion of the funds is released.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretion is a substance discharged by a gland, a bodily release.

clue.text: Au pair's modelled for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is as heard by listeners

parts.note: modelled means made, shaped or fashioned

explanation.surface: A young foreign helper does some modelling in front of a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreigner living with a family to help with childcare and housework, a household servant.

clue.text: National from Ireland downing one after drink's raised

indicators.note: after means the Ireland part follows the drink part
raised means the drink is written upwards, so backwards in a down entry

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: downing means the Ireland word swallows the next letter

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An Irish citizen downs one more after raising a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, here a citizen of an African state.

clue.text: A girl up with top down for dance

indicators.note: with top down means the topmost letter is shifted lower in the column
up means these letters are read upward, backwards in a down entry

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl gets up for a dance in a convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing A LASS gives SSALA; 'with top down' moves that first S lower, between L and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Iron dress and almost finish up like a girl

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a mini is a short dress

indicators.note: up means the trimmed word is read upwards, backwards in a down entry
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Ironing a dress and nearly finishing it is girlish work.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminine means having qualities associated with women or girls.

clue.text: Plant bug?

definitions.meaning: a stinging weed with hairy leaves
to bug is to annoy or irritate

explanation.surface: A spy asks whether to plant a listening device.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging weed and the verb meaning to irritate are spelt the same.

clue.text: Trembling creature embraces hag sharing husband

indicators.note: embraces means the creature word holds the hag word inside it

parts.note: a thing can mean a creature, as in 'poor thing'

indicators.note: the two words share one H, husband's abbreviation, so the hag word drops its own

parts.note: a hag is an old witch

explanation.surface: A shaking creature hugs an old crone, the two of them sharing a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharing husband' means the hag and the creature use one H between them, H being the abbreviation for husband, so the hag drops hers when it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitching is making small jerky movements, much like trembling or quivering.

clue.text: Master lesson in English, getting educated initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster gives a lesson in English so pupils become educated.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord, the master to whom a vassal owes service.

clue.text: Spins ends of cribbage board with pegs out

indicators.note: ends of picks the final letter of each of the two following words

parts.note: to peg out is slang for to die, so pegs out gives dies

explanation.surface: At the end of a game of cribbage the board is cleared of its pegs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cribbage is a card game scored by moving pegs along a board; 'pegs out' is also the cribbage term for winning, a neat bit of camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that eddies swirls round in circles, so it spins or whirls.

clue.text: Player pulling out all the stops?

definitions.text: Player pulling out all the stops?

parts.words: Player pulling out all the stops?
parts.note: pulling out all the stops means trying one's hardest, but literally it describes drawing every stop on a pipe organ

explanation.surface: A sportsman or performer gives it absolutely everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from the organ: pulling out every stop makes the instrument play at full volume, so the literal performer is a keyboard musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Stops are the knobs on a church organ, so the person pulling them is the musician at that instrument.

clue.text: Manoeuvre whip, drawn back with jerk

indicators.note: drawn back means the whip word is written backwards

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip, called a cat for short
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A rider performs a move, pulling back the whip with a jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned move or ploy used to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Breathes in allure with a personal appeal

indicators.note: in means the breathing word goes inside the allure word

parts.note: charm is allure or attractiveness
something that breathes lives, that is, it is or exists

explanation.surface: Breathing in someone's allure gives them a personal appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is the compelling magnetism that makes a person attractive to others.

clue.text: Tick two answers, about right, put in exercise

indicators.note: in means all these letters are placed inside the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: about means the pair of answer letters goes around the right letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer, so two of them give AA
to sit something somewhere is to put or place it

explanation.surface: A teacher ticks two answers as right and sets them down in a PE lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' looks like a mark of approval, but it is the bloodsucking mite.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a bloodsucking creature that lives off a host, the textbook example of a parasite.

clue.text: Silver jar containing a vicar's first incense

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: containing means the jar word holds the next letters

parts.note: to jar and to grate both mean to irritate

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of vicar's

explanation.surface: A silver vessel holds a vicar's incense for church.
explanation.walkthrough: Incense looks like the church perfume, but it is the verb meaning to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious, which is to annoy or exasperate them.

clue.text: Heartless to bury without 'Amen', heartless

indicators.note: without means outside, so the bury word surrounds the next part

parts.note: to inhume is to bury, the opposite of exhume

indicators.note: heartless means the central letters of Amen are removed

explanation.surface: Burying someone without saying Amen is a heartless act.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartless act is cruel and lacking compassion, the opposite of humane.

clue.text: Beetle, with another insect seizing end of horn, not moving

indicators.note: seizing means the two insects hold the next letter between them

parts.note: the stag beetle is a large horned beetle
an ant is another insect

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of horn

explanation.surface: A beetle and an ant grapple over a horn and neither budges.
explanation.walkthrough: The stag beetle's jaws look like antlers, which makes 'horn' feel part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still and does not flow, so it is motionless.

clue.text: Detective's hard behind tramp possessing Ecstasy

indicators.note: behind means the hard letter comes after the rest
possessing means the tramp word holds the drug letter

parts.note: a tramp is a derogatory word for a promiscuous woman
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough detective lurks behind a vagrant who is carrying drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, from the old word for a sleuthhound that tracks a scent.

clue.text: Go back taking first right for exit

indicators.note: taking first means the opening letter, the one for right, is taken away

parts.note: to regress is to go back to an earlier state

explanation.surface: A driver reverses and takes the first right turn to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is a way out or the act of going out, like a door or a departure.

clue.text: One backing track's ringing hollow notes

indicators.note: ringing means the track word encircles the next letters

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal

indicators.note: hollow means only the outer letters of notes remain

explanation.surface: A record producer's track rings with hollow musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is someone who backs a person or event financially, a supporter.

clue.text: Ending record, single record by Posh Spice finally

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
U means upper-class, posh in old British slang

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Spice

explanation.surface: The finale of a pop career: one last single cut by Posh Spice.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh Spice was Victoria Beckham's name in the Spice Girls; here Posh gives U, a dated British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing section added to the end of a book or play.

clue.text: Repeatedly showing temper, having lost head

indicators.note: having lost head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: showing temper in the sense of tempering, moderating something, is to soften it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps losing their temper and their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something often means doing it many times, frequently.

clue.text: Spectacle on the wagon in army spectacles

indicators.note: in means the teetotal letters sit inside the army and spectacles letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
OO looks like a pair of glasses
TT means teetotal, off the drink

explanation.surface: A sober soldier in his glasses watches a military show.
explanation.walkthrough: A military tattoo, like the famous Edinburgh one, is a display of marching bands and drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is an outdoor military show of music and drilling put on for spectators.

clue.text: Internet worm?

parts.note: a worm is a self-spreading computer program, but also a contemptible person; an online provocateur is the second kind

explanation.surface: A question about a piece of malicious software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worm' suggests computer viruses; it means a nasty person, and the nasty person who stirs up trouble online has a name from Norse folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who posts deliberately provocative messages online is a contemptible pest of the web.

clue.text: Smell starts to spread stemming from big cheese

parts.note: BO is body odour, a smell

indicators.note: starts to means taking the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A pong begins to spread from a large cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is slang for an important person in charge, a chief.

clue.text: Woo time after time without love

indicators.note: after means the first time letter follows the trimmed second one
without means the love letter is removed

parts.note: tempo is musical time or pace
love is zero in tennis, written O
tempo is musical time or pace

explanation.surface: A suitor courts again and again, though no love comes of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To woo is to try to win someone over, much as to tempt is to entice or lure them.

clue.text: Ace talent penning old hit in comeback's unusual

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: penning means the talent word encloses the following letters

parts.note: nous is good sense or know-how

indicators.note: in comeback means the hit word is turned round

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike

explanation.surface: A star performer's return to the charts with an old hit is out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anomalous departs from the norm, so it is irregular or odd.

clue.text: In printer's, tell arbitrarily between Sun and Star?

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A typesetter is told to arrange something at random.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside printer's and ends with the first two letters of arbitrarily. The Sun is itself a star, so space between it and another star is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Interstellar describes what lies in the space separating stars, and our Sun is one.
